title: Browser rendering and performance evidence
outcome: Separate network, JavaScript, layout, paint, and rendering costs before optimizing a screen.
useCase: Large workspaces, slow devices, and measurable frontend improvements.
benefits: Optimization effort follows observed user delay.
drawbacks: Lab recordings must be paired with representative conditions and regressions.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: Measure a task. Fix the costly boundary. Measure again.

trace.title: Representative task
trace.detail: A slow screen can wait on a network response, execute too much JavaScript, repeatedly measure layout, paint a large area, or render too many DOM nodes. Each needs different evidence. A fast SQL query does not prove a fast interaction.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Record open-ticket → filter → select → edit using the same fixture. Mark request start/end and visible response. Inspect long tasks, style/layout, paints, and component updates. Check the slow path after the proposed repair.

Virtualizing a list reduces DOM work but changes focus, search, row sizing, and screen-reader behavior. Memoization can add invalidation complexity. Choose the smallest fix supported by the recording.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Optimizing only the bundle can leave a long interaction unchanged. A desktop-only recording can hide low-end-device delay. A synthetic score is not the same as every real user outcome.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Separate network, JavaScript, layout, paint, and rendering costs before optimizing a screen. Explain one example and one failure.
